clue.text: Inclined to be friendly, swops ill deed for new

indicators.note: swapping the words for new ones tells us to rearrange their letters afresh

explanation.surface: Someone friendly at heart trades a bad deed for a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for new' is the anagram signal: the letters of SWOPS ILL DEED are made new.
explanation.definitionFit: Being favourably inclined towards someone is a synonym of being amicable.

clue.text: Prosperity with mostly fine food

indicators.note: most of the word, so the final letter is dropped from the synonym for fine

parts.note: fine as in 'I'm well'
fare is food, as in bill of fare

explanation.surface: Wealth comes with plenty of good food.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is wellbeing or good fortune, a synonym of prosperity.

clue.text: Tag that's left on the first person killed

parts.note: in Genesis Abel, slain by Cain, is the first murder victim

explanation.surface: A toe tag attached to the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag tied to an item naming it is a ticket or marker of identification.

clue.text: The lower classes write music? Rot

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
to compose is to write music

explanation.surface: A question whether working-class people can write music, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades social classes A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so D and E are the lowest. 'Rot' looks like a scornful comment but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay, break down into constituent parts.

clue.text: A garden pest that's shot

definitions.meaning: a shell-less mollusc that eats plants
a bullet, or a gulp of spirits

explanation.definitionFit: A slug is both a slimy plant-eating mollusc and a bullet or slug of whisky.

clue.text: Note found in Aida's works?

indicators.note: the note is located inside the other word

parts.note: Aida is one of the operas, so Aida's stands for 'opera's' (an example, hence the question mark)
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A question about a musical note in Verdi's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Aida, by Verdi, is an example of an opera, which the question mark flags. 'works' looks like 'compositions' but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that operates functions, which is what it does when it works.

clue.text: Animal that's no good being exported from part of the UK

indicators.note: sent out of the country, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: England is one of the four nations of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A creature of no use is shipped abroad from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope, a kind of beast.

clue.text: 'Freeze!' — from soldier on hearing of fabrications

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece follows on after the first

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: what the ear hears, so the word for fabrications is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: lies are fabrications

explanation.surface: A soldier's shout of 'Freeze!' on hearing lies being told.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze someone is to immobilise them, a synonym of paralyse.

clue.text: Put money on being followed, having lost money

indicators.note: something is missing, so a letter goes from the word

parts.note: being stalked is being followed
L stands for pound (libra), a unit of money

explanation.surface: A gambler, tailed by someone after losing cash, places a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the old abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra), the money lost from STALKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To stake is to wager or bet a sum on an outcome.

clue.text: Cobol users have no right to get into a stew!

indicators.note: to get into a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder
a letter is missing from the words

explanation.surface: Computer programmers who lack rights end up in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: COBOL is an old programming language. 'have no' takes R out of COBOL USERS; 'get into' scrambles the rest. Lobscouse is a sailors' stew from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobscouse is a meat-and-vegetable hash eaten by sailors, the origin of the nickname Scouse.

clue.text: Stop a good man who's after the good book

indicators.note: the man comes behind the book in the answer

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
ST, saint, is crossword shorthand for a good man

explanation.surface: Halt a righteous man who is chasing the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical command meaning cease or hold.

clue.text: Burning for a loud, dissolute male

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: loose-living, so the letters loosen and rearrange

explanation.surface: A passionate fire for a loud, debauched man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire is ablaze, alight.

clue.text: Feature earth mother with rake, oddly

parts.note: land is earth, ground
ma is mother

indicators.note: the first and third letters, the odd positions, are picked

explanation.surface: Mother Earth's garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' here is a noun: a prominent point in the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent object in the landscape, a notable feature.

clue.text: Scientist has the team back working

indicators.note: read backwards, so the word for team is turned round

parts.note: a side is a team
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A scientist has his team back at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIDE into EDIS. Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was a famous inventor, an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Might it describe paperweight as two words?

definitions.text: Might it describe paperweight as two words?

parts.words: Might it describe paperweight as two words?
parts.note: split as 'paper weight', it asks for a word naming both a traditional sheet size and a non-metric system of weights

explanation.walkthrough: Imperial is an old British paper size and also the old British system of weights (pounds and ounces), so it describes both 'paper' and 'weight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial names a large paper format and the pounds-and-ounces measure system.

clue.text: Paid for dome that's without merit and shabby

indicators.note: lacking, so letters are taken away from the word

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
frayed means worn and shabby

explanation.surface: Money spent on a worthless, tatty cupola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes OM (Order of Merit, a British honour) from DOME to leave DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray is to settle the cost, so defrayed means met the expense of.

clue.text: Indignant nurse left following reorganisation

indicators.note: the letters are organised again in a new order

explanation.surface: An angry nurse left after a shake-up at the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling resentment is being aggrieved, offended at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Tries to find bridges to support empty stage

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the one above
with its insides removed, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: arches are bridges, spans

explanation.surface: Bridges shore up an unused theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty stage' leaves S and E; in a down clue ARCHES 'support' them by sitting below.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to look for or hunt something.

clue.text: Exhausted, quietly went in to cancel day

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the word for cancel

parts.note: to delete is to cancel
p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Worn out, someone crept in quietly to call off the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted supplies are used up or drained.

clue.text: Finish supporting almost skilful back

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the upper one
not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: deft means skilful
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A nearly skilful finish from a full-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DEFT to DEF; END goes below it. 'back' looks like a football position but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a cause is to support it, to stand up for it.

clue.text: Regard, at last close encounters is back!

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken
read backwards, so the word for encounters is turned round

parts.note: meets is a synonym of encounters

explanation.surface: A fan rejoicing that Close Encounters is back in cinemas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' turns MEETS into STEEM; E is the last letter of 'close'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to respect them.

clue.text: This swimmer's crew had a supporter of course

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
on a golf course the tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A swimmer whose crew had a supporter, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but means 'on a golf course'.
explanation.definitionFit: A manatee is a sea cow, a large aquatic mammal that swims.

clue.text: Scientific study encompassing many branches

parts.note: reads like a broad academic discipline but the branches are literal ones, on trees

explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the science of managing woodland, which is full of tree limbs.

clue.text: Girl situating America between the poles

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside, flanked by the two letters

parts.note: S and N, south and north poles
America gives USA

explanation.surface: A girl placing America between the North and South Poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a female given name, standing for any girl.

clue.text: Complete agreement that Whitsun is one part of it

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters in the words

explanation.surface: A claim that Whitsun belongs within a holiday agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across wHITSUN IS ONe.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in perfect accord, all together.

clue.text: Abolish credit in advance

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages

explanation.surface: Cancel credit given ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB is British for an advance payment against wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel or scrap it.

clue.text: A race that blossom on top of Andes

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom

indicators.note: the topmost, first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A race whose flowers grow atop the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY is hawthorn blossom. The Maya lived in Central America, not the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maya are a Central American people, a race.

clue.text: Gets close to unquantified number of listeners

parts.note: n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number
ears are listeners

explanation.surface: An audience of indefinite size draws near.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to approach it.

clue.text: How a diver should get in top gear, for example

definitions.text: How a diver should get in

parts.note: the head is the top
first is an example of a car gear

explanation.surface: Advice on diving and getting a car into first gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Diving in head first means plunging forward with the head leading.

clue.text: Allies ban USA's renegotiation as being out of reach

indicators.note: the terms are worked out again, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Allies redraw a treaty banning America, leaving it untouchable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unassailable cannot be attacked or reached, impregnable.
